m.git.missing: git is not installed or not on PATH
m.git.missing.fix: Install Git for Windows and make sure `git` is on PATH.
m.repo.obtain.fix: Check the URL, your network connection and repository access.
m.repo.fsck.bad: git object database is corrupt or inconsistent
m.repo.fsck.fix: Re-clone the repository; if the problem persists the source may have been tampered with.
m.tag.missing.fix: Check the tag name; a release without a git tag cannot be tied to source.
m.tag.nokey: {tag} → {commit} (signed with key {key}, which is not in your keyring)
m.tag.sig.fix: Import the maintainer's public key (gpg --import) and re-run to verify the tag signature.
m.sum.none: no published checksums to compare against; hashes recorded
m.sum.none.fix: Publish SHA256SUMS next to the release assets so users can verify downloads.
m.sum.mismatch: {n} artifact(s) do not match the published checksum
m.sum.mismatch.cause: The downloaded file differs from what the publisher's checksum file declares.
m.sum.mismatch.fix: Re-download the artifact. If it still mismatches, the release may be corrupted or tampered with.
m.sum.nolisted: checksum file does not list any supplied artifact
m.sig.unavailable: signature present but could not be verified on this system
m.sig.invalid.cause: The signature does not validate against the file or is not trusted by this system.
m.sig.invalid.fix: Do not distribute this artifact. Re-sign it, or check that the signing certificate chain is trusted.
m.sig.warn.fix: Sign release binaries (Authenticode on Windows, GPG/minisign detached signatures elsewhere).
m.prov.gh: attestation cryptographically verified by `gh attestation verify`
m.prov.none.fix: Generate SLSA provenance (e.g. actions/attest-build-provenance) and attach it to the release.
m.prov.unbound: attestation does not cover the artifact bytes
m.prov.unbound.cause: The provenance was issued for different files than the ones supplied.
m.prov.commit: attested source commit differs from the tag's commit
m.prov.unsigned: attestation digests match the artifacts, but its signature was not verified
m.prov.unsigned.fix: Install the GitHub CLI and run with a GitHub repository to verify attestations cryptographically (`gh attestation verify`).
m.sbom.none.fix: Publish a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM with the release (cargo-cyclonedx, syft, cdxgen…).
m.sbom.invalid: SBOM present but not valid CycloneDX/SPDX
m.sbom.summary: {format} {spec} in {origin}: {n} components ({v} with version, {l} with license)
m.repro.ambiguous: cannot tell which release artifact the rebuild corresponds to
m.repro.ambiguous.fix: Name the rebuilt file identically to the release artifact.
m.repro.same: REPRODUCIBLE — rebuilt artifact is bit-for-bit identical
m.repro.diff.fix: Pin toolchain versions, strip timestamps and absolute paths (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, path remapping), then rebuild.
m.repro.nodiff: NOT REPRODUCIBLE — hashes differ (detailed analysis unavailable)
cause.embedded_path: Differing bytes contain machine-specific absolute paths (build directory leaked into the binary).
cause.pe.layout: Section layout differs; the images were not produced by the same link.
cause.pe.timestamp: PE header TimeDateStamp differs: the linker embedded the build time. Use a deterministic linker mode (e.g. /Brepro, -Wl,--no-insert-timestamp).
cause.pe.pdb_path.leaked: Debug info (PDB path) contains a machine-specific path. Build from the same directory or remap paths (/PATHMAP, --remap-path-prefix).
cause.pe.debug_guid: CodeView debug GUID/age differs (a non-deterministic PDB identity).
cause.pe.signature: Only one of the images carries an Authenticode signature; compare the unsigned content (signature is appended after the build).
cause.elf.build_id: GNU build-id differs — a consequence of any content difference, not a root cause.
cause.elf.debug: Most differing bytes ({pct}%) are in debug section {section}.
cause.zip.only_release: Entry {name} exists only in the release artifact.
cause.zip.only_local: Entry {name} exists only in the local build.
cause.zip.mtime: {n} entries have identical content but different modification times.
cause.zip.order: Archive entries are in a different order (non-deterministic file enumeration).
cause.zip.container: All entries match; only container bytes (compression level/metadata) differ.
m.docs.missing: no section found in the README or docs at this tag
m.docs.fix.install: Add an "Installation" section to the README.
m.docs.fix.usage: Add a "Usage" section with a minimal example.
m.docs.fix.upgrade: Add "Upgrading" instructions (or UPGRADING.md) describing how to move from the previous release.
m.rel.norelease: no GitHub Release exists for tag {tag}
m.rel.norelease.fix: Publish a GitHub Release for this tag with the installer/archives, checksums and SBOM attached.
m.rel.empty: the GitHub Release has no assets
m.ship.nopackage: no package was supplied for ShipCheck
m.ship.noagent: releaseverity-agent.exe was not found next to ReleaseVerity
m.ship.noagent.fix: Reinstall ReleaseVerity, or set RELEASEVERITY_AGENT to the agent's path.
m.ship.needs-windows: ShipCheck runs Windows packages and needs Windows
m.ship.host-disabled: host execution is disabled: running an untrusted installer here could modify this machine
m.ship.host-disabled.fix: Use the windows-sandbox environment, or opt in with `releaseverity config set security.allow_host_execution true` for software you trust.
m.ship.ac-installer: the built-in sandbox (appcontainer) runs portable packages only; installers must write Program Files and HKLM
m.ship.ac-installer.fix: Test installers in a VM-backed environment: --env windows-sandbox (Windows Pro/Enterprise), or use the ReleaseVerity GitHub Action on a clean runner.
m.ship.sandbox-missing: Windows Sandbox is not enabled on this machine
m.ship.sandbox-missing.fix: Enable it (Windows 10/11 Pro, Enterprise or Education): Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName Containers-DisposableClientVM, then reboot.
m.ship.sandbox-busy: another Windows Sandbox session is already open (only one can run at a time)
m.ship.sandbox-busy.fix: Close the open Windows Sandbox window and try again.
m.ship.sandbox-blocked: Windows Sandbox blocked the ReleaseVerity test agent: {why}
m.ship.sandbox-blocked.sac: Smart App Control is enforcing inside Windows Sandbox, so only signed, reputable programs may run there
m.ship.sandbox-blocked.policy: an Application Control policy inside Windows Sandbox refused to start the test agent
m.ship.sandbox-blocked.fix: Unsigned software cannot be tested in Windows Sandbox on this Windows version. Use --env appcontainer (ReleaseVerity's built-in sandbox, portable packages), a Hyper-V VM without Smart App Control, or the ReleaseVerity GitHub Action on a clean runner; or code-sign the package and agent.
m.ship.sandbox-noboot: Windows Sandbox did not start the test agent within 5 minutes
m.ship.sandbox-noboot.fix: Make sure virtualization is enabled in the BIOS and that no other Sandbox session is open.
m.ship.timeout: the environment run exceeded its overall time limit and was terminated
m.ship.noreport: the agent finished without writing a report
m.ship.smoke-notrun: not run: the application was not installed
m.ship.incomplete: the environment agent ended before this step ran
m.ship.diag.install-exit.fix: Open the log below; for MSI packages exit code 1603 means a Windows Installer error. Verify the silent-install switches (--installer-args).
m.ship.diag.crash: The process terminated with an unhandled exception (NTSTATUS crash code).
m.ship.diag.crash.fix: Reproduce under a debugger or collect a crash dump; check missing runtime dependencies (e.g. VC++ Redistributable).
m.ship.diag.hung: The application's window stopped processing messages.
m.ship.diag.hung.fix: Capture a dump while hung; look for a blocked UI thread or a startup deadlock.
m.ship.diag.timeout: The step did not finish within its time limit and its process tree was terminated.
m.ship.diag.timeout.fix: Increase the timeout (config timeouts.*) if the step is legitimately slow, otherwise investigate a deadlock or an interactive prompt.
m.ship.diag.exitcode: The process returned an unexpected exit code.
m.ship.diag.exitcode.fix: Run the command manually and inspect its output.
a.sandbox.no-installer: installers cannot run inside an AppContainer: they must write Program Files and HKLM
a.sandbox.create-fail: could not create the AppContainer sandbox: {err}
a.install.reboot: installed (a reboot is required to finish)
a.files.noentry: application found at {exe} but no Add/Remove Programs entry was registered
a.files.none: the installer reported success but no installed application could be found
a.files.noexe: no executable found in the portable package
a.launch.hung: APPLICATION HUNG — its window stopped responding
a.launch.nowindow: process stayed alive but no visible window was created
a.launch.early0: exited with code 0 before the alive window elapsed (expected a GUI to keep running)
a.uninstall.none: no uninstaller is registered (no Add/Remove Programs entry)
a.uninstall.left-files: the uninstaller exited successfully but the application files are still present
a.uninstall.left-reg: the uninstaller exited successfully but its Add/Remove Programs entry is still registered
a.uninstall.leftovers: uninstalled, but {n} leftover item(s) remain in the install directory
a.uninstall.ok: uninstalled cleanly (files and registry entry removed)
a.timeout: TEST TIMEOUT — still running after {secs}s; the process tree was terminated
a.hint.msi.1601: Windows Installer service is not accessible
a.hint.msi.1603: fatal error during installation (see the MSI log)
a.hint.msi.1618: another installation is already in progress
a.hint.msi.1620: the installation package could not be opened
a.hint.msi.1625: installation is forbidden by system policy
a.hint.msi.1638: another version of this product is already installed
a.hint.msi.default: Windows Installer returned an error (see the MSI log)
a.hint.exe.1: installer reported a generic failure or invalid command line (check the silent-install switches)
a.hint.exe.2: installation cancelled or setup failed to initialise
a.hint.exe.default: the installer returned a non-zero exit code
